lesson_title: Everyone in the Taxi Pays: Laws of Exponents
hook_text: The number in the bracket rides free? Not in this taxi. That's where your marks went.
clip_script: Start with the bracket, and here is the rule that rescues more marks than any other in this grade: when a bracket takes a power, everyone riding inside pays the fare. Nobody travels free. Three passengers sit in this taxi — the three, the x, and the y squared — so all three get squared. Three squared is nine. X squared is x squared. Y squared, squared, is y to the four — repeat the pile. The bracket becomes nine x squared y to the four. The classic error lets the three ride unsquared, and the marker spots that fare-dodger instantly.
visual_style: A minibus taxi with three cartoon passengers — a 3, an x, and a y² — each tapping a fare card that stamps a square onto them, while a fare-dodging 3 gets caught at the door in red.
pacing: Quick boarding scene, three rhythmic fare taps, a comedy beat on the dodger, clean answer landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and take the monster expression down to 3 over x squared.
